title: Load Sculptor: deterministic customer-profile generator for VPC/on-prem benchmarks
creator: Ana Patel
body:
Summary:
We need a deterministic, telemetry-driven load generator ("Load Sculptor") that can synthesize customer traffic profiles for VPC and on‑prem testbeds. The goal is reproducible tokens/sec and p95 latency curves across repeated runs so we can detect regressions in the serving runtime and network/topology interactions. This ticket covers design, implementation, and an initial validation against two customer traces (an embedding-heavy SaaS workload and a chat-heavy support workload).

Motivation and scope:
- Current replay tools mirror request events but diverge due to traffic shuffling, non-deterministic inter-arrival timing, and missing KV-cache warmup. That leads to noisy metrics and false positives in regression detection.
- Load Sculptor will: synthesize deterministic distributions for request size (tokens), concurrency, inter-arrival jitter, sequence-length buckets, and KV cache warmup patterns; provide network emulation knobs (latency, jitter, bandwidth) for VPC/on-prem parity; snapshot environment topology (node counts, GPU types, topology map) for reproducible runs.

Key metrics to produce and track (output from a run):
- tokens_per_sec: aggregated and per-worker time series (1s granularity)
- p95_latency_ms: end-to-end request p95 measured at the ingress gateway and at the model runtime
- success_rate: success vs retry vs error rates per route
- kv_cache_hit_rate: prefix/KV warmup curve over the run
- queue_depth and batch_size distribution: continuous histograms
- regression_score: computed metric combining p95 and tokens/sec deltas (see detection rules)

Regression detection rules (initial):
- Short-term alert: if p95 increases > 15% and tokens_per_sec decreases > 10% within a 5-minute sliding window -> open regression investigation ticket automatically.
- Sustained regression: if deviation persists > 30 minutes -> escalate to oncall and create incident template populated with artifacts.
- Statistical guard: for noisy workloads apply bootstrap confidence intervals over baseline runs (N=5) and require change to be outside 95% CI to count as regression.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Deterministic seeds vs true replay: we purposely synthesize from fingerprinted distributions (token length histogram, route ratios, actor concurrency) rather than byte-for-byte replay. This gives higher reproducibility across environment differences but can omit edge-case timing found in raw traces.
- KV-cache warmup modeling: we model warmup as staged cohorts (hot prefixes, warm prefixes, cold prefixes) derived from trace frequency and then schedule early-phase warmup requests. This is heavier than naive replay but essential to match steady-state tokens/sec and p95.
- Network emulation: prefer use of standard linux 'tc/netem' profiles and a lightweight cross-platform wrapper (netemctl) to avoid dependency on heavy simulator infra. We capture egress/ingress latency distributions from customer VPC tests and translate to netem params.

Implementation plan and components:
1) Fingerprint extractor (go/python): ingest a trace (pcap/http logs) and output a fingerprint JSON: route blend, token_length_histogram, prefix-frequency list, concurrency profile, inter-arrival baseline.
2) Sculptor engine (rust): deterministic workload generator that reads fingerprint JSON + seed and emits scheduled requests with stable timing. Support for: rate shaping, burst shaping, concurrency targets, KV warmup cohorts.
3) Topology snapshotter (python/cli): records cluster config (node types, GPU counts, runtime version, kernel selection hints), stores as 'env-snapshot' file to reproduce topology.
4) Runner and validator (bash/python): orchestrates a run in a VPC or on‑prem lab, applies netem profiles, uploads telemetry to our metrics endpoint, and computes classification metrics and regression_score.

Progress updates (so far):
- 2026-02-10: prototype fingerprint extractor implemented; extracts route ratios and token histograms from sample customer trace A (chat). Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Load+Sculptor+Fingerprinting.
- 2026-02-22: sculptor engine POC emits deterministic schedules that reproduce per-second token curves within +/-4% on local single-node runs. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench/pull/389.
- 2026-03-03: implemented KV warmup cohorts and verified p95 stabilization after warmup window (10–15 minutes) on our lab cluster. Validation dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/bench/loads_sculptor_validation.
- 2026-03-08: integrated netemctl wrappers and validated VPC-replay parity on staged customer-like topology (added 12ms median latency, 2ms jitter).

How to run a canonical benchmark (example):
- generate fingerprint: ./tools/fingerprint-extractor --input traces/customerA.log --output traces/customerA.fp.json
- create env snapshot: ./tools/toposnap --output snapshots/custA-20260308.env.json --cluster kube:5:g4dn.xlarge --runtime runtime-1.21
- run sculptor (deterministic): ./bin/load-sculptor run --fingerprint traces/customerA.fp.json --env snapshots/custA-20260308.env.json --seed 1729 --duration 60m --netem profiles/custA.latency
- collect artifacts: ./bin/load-sculptor collect --run-id <id> --dest ./artifacts/<id>/
- compute summary: ./tools/summary --artifacts ./artifacts/<id>/ --output ./artifacts/<id>/summary.json

Acceptance criteria:
- Reproducibility: repeated runs (N=3) on the same env snapshot must have tokens_per_sec mean within 5% and p95 within 10% across runs after warmup period.
- Regression sensitivity: injected controlled slowdown (kernel slowdown or forced GC) should trigger short-term alert rules above.
- Trace fidelity: for two customer traces provided we achieve similar steady-state KV cache hit curves (within 8 percentage points).

Test plan and validation matrix:
- Workloads: chat-heavy (short prompts, many small responses), embed-heavy (long prompts, high token counts), mixed enterprise (long/short blend).
- Envs: single-node on‑prem lab, 3-node VPC neptune-like topology, customer-like topology with 50ms WAN links.
- Metrics: tokens/sec (1s bins), p50/p95/p99, batch size distribution, KV hit curves.

Open blockers and risks:
- Trace anonymization: some customer traces include PII; need legal sign-off for ingestion. Owner: Legal.
- Netem coverage: emulating complex cloud network effects (packet loss patterns at scale) might not map perfectly to netem. We may need to extend with synthetic packet loss models.
- Long warmups: some workloads need >30 minutes to reach steady state; run cost could be substantial on dedicated hardware. Need cost estimate.

Next steps (short term):
- Finish rust sculptor engine feature parity: route weights and cohort-based warmup scheduling (target 2026-03-15).
- Add automated regression detector and hook it into alerts on staging cluster (2026-03-18).
- Run 3 canonical benchmarks for both customer traces and publish validation report to confluence (2026-03-20).

Artifacts and references:
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Load+Sculptor+Design
- GitHub PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench/pull/389, https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench/pull/412
- Validation dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/bench/loads_sculptor_validation

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus review on the regression detection thresholds and bootstrap approach. We set conservative defaults but need product input on acceptable alert noise.
- Also validate whether the env snapshot collects sufficient kernel/runtime knobs (cuda drivers, kernel version) for faithful reproduction in customer on‑prem environments.

Comments/updates timeline:
- 2026-03-09 (Marcus Li): "Added per-worker batch_size histograms and an option to emit synthetic tail requests to exercise long-prompt codepaths."
- 2026-03-10 (Ana Patel): "Validated tokens/sec reproducibility on 3 runs for sample A: mean delta 3.6%, p95 delta 9.1% after 12m warmup — meets acceptance so far."

If blocked: contact Marcus Li or Ana Patel.
